summary: This script scans a folder, categorizes files by type (code, config, docs, etc.), and generates a pie chart visualization showing the distribution of file types. It walks through the directory structure, counts files in each category, formats the data for Mermaid (a charting library), and runs a command-line tool to render it as an image.

explanations.6: os.path.splitext splits a filename into the name and extension parts, then [1] grabs just the extension (the part after the dot), and .lower() makes it lowercase so '.PY' matches '.py'.
explanations.22: dirs[:] = [...] modifies the list in-place; this tells os.walk to skip hidden folders (starting with a dot) and Python cache folders, so they won't be descended into.
explanations.26: counts.get(cat, 0) safely retrieves the count for this category, defaulting to 0 if it doesn't exist yet, so we can add 1 without an error on the first occurrence.
explanations.29: This returns a minimal Mermaid pie chart syntax when the folder has no files, so the script doesn't crash and still produces valid output.
explanations.46: os.path.abspath converts a relative path (like '.') into a full absolute path, ensuring consistent behavior regardless of what directory the user runs the script from.
explanations.54: subprocess.run executes an external command (mmdc, the Mermaid CLI tool) with specific arguments to convert the .mmd file into a PNG image with custom styling.
explanations.62: After the pie chart is generated, we delete the temporary .mmd file since it's no longer needed.
